Date: 2026-04-02

Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Menon (Redwood SE), Michael Rivera (Cerulean), Anika Shah (Cerulean), Tom Becker (Cerulean)
summary: Redwood product walkthrough focused on data handling and retention controls: logging redaction, PII masking, request storage toggles, and audit logs. Customer concerned about bank regulatory requirements, data residency, and ability to disable request storage for hosted API. Agreed next steps: send security docs, share console screenshots, and schedule pilot benchmark with sample volumes.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan, AE at Redwood, and Priya our SE is with me. Quick intro then we'll jump into a demo of the Console and the data retention controls.
[02:12] Michael Rivera: Hey Jordan, thanks. We've got a few folks on from security and platform. Short context: bank, regulated, need strict PII handling, and want to understand hosted API vs Dedicated or private VPC options.
[04:30] Priya Menon: Great, thanks Michael. I'll share my screen — bear with me, getting the Console up. So first, on the API level we provide request_storage toggles per-api-key or per-route — you can disable request storage entirely which means we won't persist request/response bodies in our long-term logs.
[06:05] Anika Shah: When you say 'disable request storage', is that for hosted as well or only for Dedicated/Private? Any residual metadata retained?
[07:40] Priya Menon: Good q. For hosted API you can opt out of storing full request/response payloads; we still capture minimal telemetry for billing and SLOs (latency/tokens), but we can redact or hash any PII fields before persisting. For Dedicated/Private, you control logs fully and can push logs to your S3 or on-prem logging. Note: metadata we keep is very small and can be configured — request id, timestamp, model, token counts.
[09:10] Tom Becker: And is that metadata stored encrypted? KMS? Customer managed keys?
[10:25] Jordan Lee: Yes, everything at rest is encrypted. For Private deployments and enterprise Dedicated we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). For hosted we use our KMS by default but can arrange bring-your-own-key in contract.
[12:00] Michael Rivera: We need audit trails for compliance — retention, who accessed logs, and immutable audit logs. Do you provide that?
[13:20] Priya Menon: Absolutely. Console shows audit logs with RBAC and SSO integration (SAML/OIDC). We include user, action, timestamp, IP. Audit logs themselves can be exported to SIEMs or long-term storage.
[15:05] Jordan Lee: I'm going to show the redaction tooling — small caveat, the agent here might say 'optimized' but sometimes timestamps glint — apologies for any mic fuzz.
[16:20] Priya Menon: (screen) In the Console under Security > Data Controls, you can define field-level redaction rules. You can upload regexes or JSON path selectors, and those rules run at ingestion time so PII never lands in logs. There's also a 'sanitize mode' to replace with placeholders like [REDACTED] or hashed values.
[18:45] Anika Shah: Can we test rules against a sample set? Need to make sure we don't over-redact numeric tokens (acct numbers) or under-redact.
[20:00] Priya Menon: Yes — the Console has a sandbox where you paste sample payloads and see the transformed output. I'll paste an example. (typing) You'll see account numbers masked, names redacted, and email addresses hashed.
[21:30] Michael Rivera: How reliable is the auto-detection? Do you use ML for PII detection or purely rule-based? We worry about free-text fields.
[22:50] Priya Menon: It's a hybrid. There's regex and rules for structured data plus an ML-backed PII detector tuned for LLM inputs; both run and you can set precedence. For regulated data we recommend explicit rules and a conservative policy.
[24:15] Tom Becker: About request storage toggles — if we disable storage, can we still run quality monitoring and evals? We rely on sample logs for drift detection.
[25:40] Jordan Lee: Short answer: yes, but with tradeoffs. You can enable ephemeral logging where samples are stored for a short retention window (e.g., 7 days) for evals, then auto-delete. Alternatively, key routes can write hashed or pseudonymized transcripts to a separate secure bucket for evals only. Priya, can you show the retention slider?
[27:05] Priya Menon: (screen) Here — retention policy per route: 0 days (no storage), 7, 30, 90, custom. You can also set retention by data classification tag. There's an automatic scheduled purge job and we surface deletion confirmations in audit logs.
[28:50] Anika Shah: If we ask for deletion, how do you verify it's been fully deleted? Is there an attestation?
[29:55] Priya Menon: We provide deletion receipts and we can offer periodic attestations for enterprise plans. For Dedicated/Private you control the storage endpoints so standard enterprise retention practices apply.
[31:10] Michael Rivera: Performance question — does redaction add latency? We can't exceed certain API latency for real-time features.
[32:30] Priya Menon: There's minimal overhead for rule-based redaction at ingestion. For heavy ML-backed PII scanning it can add 10-30ms typically; our continuous batching and async hooks can mitigate. For ultra-low latency you can do pre-ingest client-side redaction.
[34:00] Tom Becker: Any concerns about cost? Storing everything with 90-day retention ramps costs. We want to understand cost vs retention tradeoffs and if Optimize gives suggestions.
[35:15] Jordan Lee: Redwood Optimize analyzes request patterns and suggests batching, caching and retention profiles to save costs. For example, ephemeral caching of common prefixes and recommending which routes can be 0-day retention. We can run a cost model for your sample volume during the pilot.
[36:45] Anika Shah: What about model fallback and caching — will that accidentally cause sensitive data to be cached and served to other tenants?
[37:55] Priya Menon: Great point. We isolate KV caches by tenant and by model instance. There's no cross-tenant leakage. For private we zone caches in your VPC. We also redact keys used in caches where possible.
[39:20] Michael Rivera: Ok, sounds promising. A few internal blockers: legal wants a clear statement we won't surface customer PII in logs; security wants to run an inbound pentest and review the audit implementation.
[40:40] Jordan Lee: Totally reasonable. We'll share the security pack (SOC2, ISO certs), the redaction whitepaper, and set up a pentest process. We can also set up a short pilot on Dedicated or Private trial depending on your preference.
[41:55] Tom Becker: Timeline-wise, if we sign up for a pilot, how fast can we get a Dedicated pool or Private demo?
[42:40] Priya Menon: Dedicated pools can be provisioned in 2-4 weeks typically; Private demo depends on networking but we can do a VPC-connected trial in a similar timeframe. Hosted pilot can start immediately with request_storage toggles enabled.
[43:30] Michael Rivera: OK let's recap. Jordan?
[44:00] Jordan Lee: Recap: we'll send SOC2/ISO docs, the redaction demo recording and Console screenshots, and sample retention configs. Customer to share volume estimates and any specific legal questions. We'll aim to kick off a pilot next week subject to paperwork. Thanks everyone.
[44:30] Meeting ended.
